meaning:
σείω
[in LXX chiefly for רָעַשׁ ;]
to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, Heb.12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Mat.27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Rev.6:13. Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Mat.21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”
whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens.”
The stars of the sky fell to the earth, like a fig tree dropping its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind.
